script.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.

terra.problem: Jacob being Isaac's son is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference, such as Genesis 25:26.
Jacob says he wants to return home, but the passage does not say he is packing.
Jacob asks for his wives and children, but he does not name them here. The passage also does not yet show them leaving with him.
Jacob does not ask for his family by name, and the passage does not yet show them leaving with him.
The explanation assumes a warning would make Laban want Jacob gone and states exactly why Laban wants him to stay. The text does not say either.
Laban asks Jacob to stay, but the passage does not say the result is that Jacob stays.
The passage does not say the animals Jacob names have less common colors.
Jacob specifies goats that are not speckled or spotted and lambs that are not dark-colored. Saying any animal that does not match would be considered stolen broadens his statement.
The passage says Laban removed the animals that day, not that he did it in one afternoon.
The explanation repeats that Laban's sons received the animals without adding much insight or personality.
Leah and Rachel being Jacob's wives is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference, such as Genesis 29:23, 28, 30.
The text says peeling exposed the white wood, but it does not say that exposing it was the whole point of Jacob's action.
The passage does not state that white was the color Jacob was after.
The explanation repeats that the wood was white without adding much insight or personality.
The text places branches in front of the flocks coming to drink; it does not say every animal walked past them.
The explanation repeats where the branches went without adding much insight or personality.
Jacob's stated wages do not include every streaked animal, so the explanation overstates the match between the young born and the animals he named.
Jacob's stated wages do not include every streaked animal, so the young described are not necessarily all the very animals he asked for.
The passage does not say Jacob separated his stock to make the animals easy to count.
The passage does not say all the animals came to the troughs to drink.
The explanation repeats that the animals were weak without adding much insight or personality.
The passage says Jacob became prosperous, but it does not say whether he had any debt.
